drivingQuestion: Which tanna holds that food and drink do not combine?
outcomeNote: Rav Hisda's answer is given; alternative answers follow in the next unit.

segments.he: הָאוֹכֵל וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין. מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּמַחְלוֹקֶת שְׁנוּיָה, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא. דִּתְנַן, כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כֹּל שֶׁטּוּמְאָתוֹ וְשִׁיעוּרוֹ שָׁוֶה — מִצְטָרֵף.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna that «food and drink do not combine.» The Gemara asks: «Who» is the tanna who «taught» this? «Rav Ḥisda said:» This halakha «is taught as a dispute, and» the mishna «is» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua. As we learned» in a mishna: «Rabbi Yehoshua stated a general principle: Any» item «that» is «identical» to another item in «its» type of «ritual impurity,» e.g., impurity that lasts only until evening, «and its measure» for impurity, e.g., an olive-bulk, «combines» with the other item to reach one measure to render other items impure. Therefore, two half olive-bulk pieces of two corpses or of two animal carcasses, or two half lentil-bulk pieces from two creeping animals all combine to render other items impure.
